data.narrative:
Hailo is a Series D semiconductor chip company that has raised $564M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the chip design and AI inference space, including Tenstorrent, Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, and PsiQuantum.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier, yields $846M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Etched ($5.0B, Series C), Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series C), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—produces a median of $2.4B. The peer range spans $529M to $5.0B. Public comp anchoring via P/S multiples (21.4x median across the three public tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private companies.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a valuation range of $719M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.6B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around whether Hailo's commercial traction and market position align with earlier-stage or later-stage peers. Capital raised serves as a floor; peer positioning relative to more mature competitors (e.g., Tenstorrent at $2.7B) and product-market fit visibility remain critical inputs for narrowing this band.
